# audio

Imported as `@elffuss/ai/audio`, `@elffuss/ai/audio/sizes`.

## `sdk/audio/g2p-en.js`

Follows the lexicon rules of misaki (github.com/hexgrad/misaki, misaki/en.py, Apache-2.0, by hexgrad), the phonemiser Kokoro was trained with: its US word lists (gold, then silver, both grown with capitalised forms), the -s, -ed and -ing endings, letters read one by one for acronyms, the special cases of a, an, the, to, in and I by what follows, and its stress rules. Rewritten in JavaScript without spaCy, so without part-of-speech tags: a word with several readings takes its default one. Numbers are spelt out before (numbers.js). Words the lists do not have go to the fallback (the small network of misaki, run by speech-impl.js). Pure: the lists and the fallback are passed in.

### `applyStress(ps, stress)`

misaki's apply_stress.

### `createEnglish(lists)`

An English (US) phonemiser over misaki's lists.

| Parameter | Type | |
|---|---|---|
| `lists` | `{ gold: Record<string, string\|Record<string, string\|null>>, silver: Record<string, string> }` |  |

### `englishToPhonemes(en, text, fallback)`

English text to Kokoro phonemes.

| Parameter | Type | |
|---|---|---|
| `en` | `ReturnType<typeof createEnglish>` |  |
| `text` | `string` |  |
| `fallback` | `(word: string) => Promise<string>` | phonemes of a word the lists lack |

Returns `Promise<string>`.

## `sdk/audio/g2p-es.js`

Spanish text to the phonemes Kokoro's Spanish voices were trained on. Kokoro phonemised Spanish with eSpeak NG ("es", Castilian) and a small mapping of misaki (t^ʃ → ʧ, a^ɪ → I, e^ɪ → A, a^ʊ → W); Spanish spelling is regular enough to give the same symbols by rule, so eSpeak NG (GPL) is not shipped. What the rules follow, as eSpeak NG writes it: - the stress mark goes right before the stressed vowel (after any glide), - b, d, g soften to β, ð, ɣ after a vowel or a consonant, across words too, - c/z before e, i → θ; ll → ʎ; y → ʝ (i at the end or alone); j and g before - unstressed i, u next to a vowel are glides (j, w); ai/ay → I, ei/ey → A, Pure; the tests compare it with eSpeak NG's output for a list of sentences.

### `UNSTRESSED`

Words eSpeak NG leaves unstressed.

### `SECONDARY`

Words that take a secondary stress only.

### `wordPhonemes(word, stress = 'primary')`

Phonemes of one word with B, D, G still to resolve (stop or fricative) by context.

| Parameter | Type | |
|---|---|---|
| `word` | `string` | lower case, letters only |
| `[stress]` | `'primary'\|'secondary'\|'none'` |  |

### `spanishToPhonemes(text)`

Spanish text to Kokoro phonemes.

| Parameter | Type | |
|---|---|---|
| `text` | `string` |  |

Returns `string`.

## `sdk/audio/graph-patch.js`

The SAME-S decoder of Stable Audio 3 (with its limiter) holds four scalar constants in double precision, -1, 1, -32767 and 32767, each cast to float by the next node. ONNX Runtime Web's WebGPU build has no Cast from double, so the session cannot be created. Here they become int64 constants of the same value, in place: the tensor's type field (11 → 7) and its eight bytes, so no length in the protobuf changes and Cast(int64 → float) gives exactly the same floats. Only constants laid out as `data_type: DOUBLE, raw_data: <8 bytes>` with an integral value are touched. Pure.

### `doubleScalarsToInt64(bytes, { values } = {})`

Rewrite integral double scalars of an ONNX model as int64, in place.

| Parameter | Type | |
|---|---|---|
| `bytes` | `Uint8Array` | the model |
| `[opts]` | `{ values?: number[] }` | the values allowed (all integral ones when left out) |

Returns `number`: how many were rewritten

## `sdk/audio/index.js`

Audio from text in the browser: music and sound effects with Stable Audio 3 Small (Stability AI, Stability AI Community License; its text encoder T5Gemma is also under the Gemma Terms of Use) on WebGPU, and speech: in Spanish with MOSS-TTS-Nano (OpenMOSS, Apache-2.0) on WebAssembly, in Spanish and English with Kokoro 82M (hexgrad, Apache-2.0) on WebGPU or WebAssembly. The models come from their Hugging Face repositories at pinned revisions, through the Elffuss model store. Each task class runs its model in a module Worker of this module (its URL is relative to this file, so the module can be served from any origin together with the core and the runtimes).
 The options of run() are plain JSON, so a chat or an agent can pass a tool call straight through: { prompt, seconds, seed } for music and sound effects, { text, voice, lang, speed } for speech. A run gives a WAV Blob and what it is.

### `SPEECH_MODELS`

The speech model of each family of voices.

### `VOICES`

The voices offered, Spanish first: `model` is the family that speaks it (`moss`:
MOSS-TTS-Nano, Elffuss's own voice; `kokoro`: Kokoro 82M).

### `DEFAULT_VOICE`

Default voice of each language: Elffuss's own in Spanish, Kokoro's Heart in English.

### `speechModelFor(input = {}, model)`

The model that reads a run: the voice's family; without a voice, Kokoro for
English, else `model` (the task's `model` option) or MOSS-TTS-Nano.

| Parameter | Type | |
|---|---|---|
| `input` | `{ voice?: string, lang?: string }` |  |
| `[model]` | `string` |  |

### Type `AudioResult`

```ts
{ blob: Blob, mime: 'audio/wav', seconds: number, sampleRate: number, channels: number, seed?: number, model: string, device: 'webgpu'|'wasm', dtype: string, stats: { peakDb: number, rmsDb: number, clipped: number, silent: number } } & Record<string, any>
```

What `run()` gives: `blob` is a 16-bit PCM WAV of `seconds` at `sampleRate` (44 100 Hz stereo for music and sound effects, 48 000 Hz mono for speech with Elffuss's own voice, 24 000 Hz mono with Kokoro); `seed` reproduces a music or sound clip, or a reading with Elffuss's own voice; `stats` measures it.

### Type `AudioProgress`

```ts
{ status: string, stage?: 'download'|'load'|'encode'|'step'|'decode'|'phonemes'|'text'|'chunk'|'frame', step?: number, steps?: number, chunk?: number, chunks?: number, frames?: number, loaded?: number, total?: number }
```

Progress events: `download` (loaded/total bytes), `load`, then for music and sound `encode`, `step` (step of steps) and `decode`; for speech with Kokoro `phonemes` and `chunk` (chunk of chunks); for speech with Elffuss's own voice `text`, then per chunk `chunk`, `frame` (every 5 frames of audio, 12.5 a second) and `decode`; finally status `done`.

### Type `AudioEstimate`

```ts
{ fits: boolean, reason: string|null, device: 'webgpu'|'wasm'|null, downloadBytes: number, missingBytes: number }
```

What a run would need here, without downloading anything: `reason` is null when it fits, otherwise `webgpu-unavailable`, `no-shader-f16`, `gpu-limits`, `memory` or `device-unsupported`.

### `estimateTask(task, opts = {}, device = 'auto')`

What a run of `task` would need in this browser (no download): whether it fits, and
what it would download. `opts.store` (any object with has(url, bytes)) tells what is
already in this browser; without one, everything counts as missing.

| Parameter | Type | |
|---|---|---|
| `task` | `string` |  |
| `[opts]` | `{ registry?: object, registryUrl?: string, model?: string, store?: { has(url: string, bytes: number): Promise<boolean> } }` |  |
| `[device]` | `'auto'\|'webgpu'\|'wasm'` |  |

Returns `Promise<AudioEstimate>`.

### `class Music`

Music from a text description, with Stable Audio 3 Small Music, on WebGPU with
shader-f16. The first load asks the model store for its files (about 1.8 GB,
shared with `Sfx` but its DiT) and checks their hashes.

```js
import { Music } from '@elffuss/ai/audio';
const music = new Music({ onProgress: p => console.log(p.stage, p.step, p.steps) });
const { blob, seconds, seed } = await music.run({ prompt: 'Lo-fi hip hop, mellow piano, 80 BPM', seconds: 30, seed: 7 });
await music.dispose();   // frees every WebGPU buffer and the Worker
```

`run({ prompt, seconds, seed, steps }, { signal })`: `seconds` 2 to 120 (30), `seed`
0 to 2147483647 (random when left out, and given back), `steps` 4 to 16 (8).
Resolves to an `AudioResult` (44 100 Hz stereo WAV).

- `.constructor(options)`
- `.estimate(opts, device)`: What a run would need here; see `estimateTask`.

### `class Sfx`

Sound effects from a text description, with Stable Audio 3 Small SFX, on WebGPU
with shader-f16. Same options and result as `Music`; `seconds` 0.5 to 30 (5).

- `.constructor(options)`
- `.estimate(opts, device)`: What a run would need here; see `estimateTask`.

### `class Speech`

Speech from text, in Spanish with Elffuss's own voice (MOSS-TTS-Nano, about 720 MB,
WebAssembly) or in English (and Kokoro's Spanish voices) with Kokoro 82M (WebGPU or
WebAssembly). The voice picks the model; each is loaded the first time a run needs it.
Long texts are read sentence by sentence and joined with natural pauses.

```js
import { Speech } from '@elffuss/ai/audio';
const speech = new Speech({ onProgress: p => console.log(p.stage, p.chunk, p.chunks) });
const { blob, seconds } = await speech.run({ text: '¿Te apetece un café?', lang: 'es' });
await speech.dispose();
```

`run({ text, voice, lang, speed, seed }, { signal })`: `voice` one of `VOICES` (by
default `es_elffuss` in Spanish, `af_heart` in English), `lang` 'es' or 'en' (by
default the voice's), `speed` 0.5 to 2 (Kokoro's voices; 1), `seed` (Elffuss's
voice: the same seed reads a text the same way; random when left out, and given
back). Resolves to an `AudioResult`: 48 000 Hz mono WAV with MOSS-TTS-Nano,
24 000 Hz with Kokoro, with the voice, language and chunks read.

- `.constructor(options = {})`
- `.device`: Backend of the last model used, after load() or run().
- `.dtype`: Variant dtype of the last model used.
- `.info`: What load() of the last model used returned, or null.
- `.load({ signal, lang, voice } = {})`: Load the model of a language or voice (Spanish by default) without running it.
- `.run(input, opts)`: Read a text aloud.
- `.dispose()`: Release every model loaded and their Workers. Idempotent.
- `.estimate(opts = {}, device)`: What a run would need here; see `estimateTask`. `opts.lang` or `opts.voice` picks the model (Spanish by default).

### `music`

Load, run once and dispose, for tool calls: `await music({ prompt, seconds, seed })`.
Options of the task (device, store, onProgress, signal…) may go in the same object.

### `sfx`

Load, run once and dispose: `await sfx({ prompt, seconds, seed })`. @type {typeof music}

### `speak`

Load, run once and dispose: `await speak({ text, voice, lang, speed })`.

### `audio`

The audio tools as a chat or an agent calls them: `audio.music`, `audio.sfx`, `audio.speak`.

## `sdk/audio/moss.js`

The pieces of MOSS-TTS-Nano's voice cloning that are not the model: the text as the model takes it, the chunks a long text is read in, the rows of the request (the prompt template, the voice's codes, the text's ids) and the inputs of the sampling graph. They follow the official ONNX runtime of OpenMOSS (onnx_tts_runtime.py and ort_cpu_runtime.py of OpenMOSS/MOSS-TTS-Nano, Apache-2.0), written again from what it does; no code of it is copied. Pure.

The text as the official runtime cleans it before the tokenizer (its robust

## `sdk/audio/rng.js`

Seeded random numbers for the diffusion noise: the same seed gives the same noise in every run of this module, so a seed reproduces a clip. xoshiro128** for uniform numbers (seeded through SplitMix32) and the Box-Muller transform for normal ones. Pure, no DOM.

The arithmetic of Stable Audio 3 Small around its networks, as Stability AI's own MLX pipeline does it (github.com/Stability-AI/stable-audio-3, optimized/mlx/models/defs/sa3_pipeline.py; no code is copied): the latent length of a duration, the sampling schedule (linear in t, warped through log-SNR) and one step of the ping-pong sampler of the rf_denoiser models:

 Pure, no DOM.

### `SAMPLE_RATE`

Sample rate of Stable Audio 3 (stereo).

### `SAMPLES_PER_LATENT`

### `latentLength(seconds)`

Latent positions for a duration in seconds (natural ceiling, at least 1).

### `decoderLength(length)`

The SAME-S decoder needs an even number of positions: the length it is given
(the last position repeated when needed). Its windows are local, so the
repeated position only adds audio after the end, which is cut.

log-SNR shift of t in [0, 1] (rate 0: the same for every length). Ends are kept.

## `sdk/audio/speech.impl.js`

## `sdk/audio/spm.js`

The SentencePiece tokenizer of T5Gemma (the text encoder of Stable Audio 3), read from its tokenizer.model and encoding as SentencePiece's BPE model does: spaces become ▁ (no normalisation, no dummy prefix), the text is split into characters (user-defined symbols such as <mask> kept whole), the adjacent pair whose join is a piece with the highest score is merged until none is left, and what is not a piece falls back to its UTF-8 bytes (<0xNN>). No BOS or EOS is added: Stable Audio feeds the ids as SentencePiece's Encode gives them. Pure, no DOM; written from the format, no code of SentencePiece is copied.

### `parseModel(bytes)`

Read the pieces of a SentencePiece ModelProto (field 1: piece, score, type).

### `nmtNfkc(text)`

The normaliser of a model with SentencePiece's `nmt_nfkc` rule, `remove_extra_whitespaces`
and `add_dummy_prefix` (MOSS-TTS-Nano): Unicode NFKC, control characters dropped, every
kind of space and line break as one space, the ends trimmed, and one space in front.

| Parameter | Type | |
|---|---|---|
| `text` | `string` |  |

### `createTokenizer(pieces, { normalize = null } = {})`

A tokenizer from a model's pieces.

| Parameter | Type | |

| `pieces` | `{ piece: string, score: number, type: number }[]` |  |
| `[o]` | `{ normalize?: (text: string) => string }` | `normalize`: the model's normaliser (none for T5Gemma; `nmtNfkc` for MOSS-TTS-Nano) |

Returns `{ ids: BigInt64Array, mask: BigInt64Array, count: number, truncated: boolean }`.

## `sdk/audio/stable-audio.js`

Stable Audio 3 Small (music or sound effects) where the model runs: the T5Gemma text encoder, the DiT and the SAME-S decoder of Stability AI's ONNX export, on ONNX Runtime Web (WebGPU). A run tokenises the prompt, encodes it once, draws the latent noise from the seed, takes the sampler's steps through the DiT and decodes the latent to 44.1 kHz stereo; the decoder's limiter keeps the peaks under full scale. The three sessions stay loaded between runs and are all released by dispose(). Never fetches and never touches the DOM.

### `PROMPT_TOKENS`

Tokens of the prompt the text encoder reads.

### `MAX_PROMPT`

Longest prompt accepted, in characters.

### `DURATION`

Durations each task offers, in seconds.

### `STEPS`

Steps a caller may ask for.

### `normalizeInput(task, input)`

Check and complete the options of a run.

| Parameter | Type | |
|---|---|---|
| `task` | `string` |  |
| `input` | `{ prompt?: string, seconds?: number, seed?: number, steps?: number }` |  |

### `stableAudioImpl(task)`

Implementation of one of the two tasks.

## `sdk/audio/text.js`

Long text for the speech task: sentences (with the pause that follows each), then chunks the model can read in one go. Kokoro reads at most 510 phonemes at a time and sounds best a sentence or a few at a time, so sentences are packed up to a budget, and a sentence over it is cut at a comma, a semicolon or, at worst, a space. Pure.

### `MAX_PHONEMES`

Most phonemes Kokoro takes in one pass.

### `CHUNK_PHONEMES`

Phonemes a chunk is filled up to (room for the joins).

### `pauseAfter(text, paragraphEnd = false)`

Seconds of pause after a piece that ends in this character.

### `sentences(text)`

Split text into sentences, each with the pause after it.

| Parameter | Type | |
|---|---|---|
| `text` | `string` |  |

Returns `{ text: string, pause: number }[]`.

### `cutPhonemes(ps, max = MAX_PHONEMES)`

Cut a phoneme string that is too long, at the last comma or semicolon before
the limit, else the last space, else hard.

| Parameter | Type | |
|---|---|---|
| `ps` | `string` |  |
| `[max]` | `number` |  |

Returns `string[]`.

### `packChunks(items, budget = CHUNK_PHONEMES)`

Pack phonemised sentences into chunks: whole sentences up to `budget`
phonemes; one too long is cut. Each chunk keeps the pause of its last sentence.

| Parameter | Type | |
|---|---|---|
| `items` | `{ ps: string, pause: number }[]` |  |

Returns `{ ps: string, pause: number }[]`.

## `sdk/audio/wav.js`

WAV files: 16-bit PCM (what the tasks give) or 32-bit float, read back for the page's player and history. Pure, no DOM.

### `encodeWav(channels, sampleRate, { float = false } = {})`

Encode planar channels as a WAV file.

| Parameter | Type | |
|---|---|---|
| `channels` | `Float32Array[]` | one array per channel, same length, values -1..1 |
| `sampleRate` | `number` |  |
| `[opts]` | `{ float?: boolean }` | `float`: 32-bit float instead of 16-bit PCM |

Returns `ArrayBuffer`.

### `decodeWav(buf)`

Read a WAV file (PCM 16, 24 or 32 bits, or 32-bit float).

| Parameter | Type | |
|---|---|---|
| `buf` | `ArrayBuffer` |  |

Returns `{ sampleRate: number, channels: Float32Array[] }`.
